source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-272521:Shears item use statistic ignores tool component
source_meta._title: Statistic for using shears doesn't increase when mining certain blocks

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 18w14b in a separate launcher installation or game directory; new single-player Survival world with cheats enabled. Use an ordinary generated Overworld with enough clear ground to place one carpet block. No particular seed, coordinates, difficulty, server, or additional player is specified by the report.
preconditions: The launcher can start the exact Java Edition snapshot Minecraft 18w14b.
Use a new world rather than opening an important existing world in this historical snapshot.
The world must be in Survival mode when the carpet is mined.
Cheats must be enabled because the report's scoreboard setup requires commands; this plan also uses commands to obtain deterministic test items.
Use the default attack/mine control of left-click and use/place control of right-click, or the corresponding rebound controls.
The test uses white carpet as a deterministic representative of the report's unspecified carpet color.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher profile configured for Java Edition snapshot 18w14b. At the main menu, verify that the displayed game version is 18w14b before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as 18w14b.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world. From the main menu select Singleplayer, select Create New World, leave Game Mode set to Survival, open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, then create the world. The world name and seed may be arbitrary.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Survival -> More World Options -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a new world with the Survival HUD visible, including hearts and hunger icons.

steps.action: Wait before issuing commands or placing the test block. Continue only after nearby terrain has rendered and movement and camera controls respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The spawn-area chunks are rendered and the player can move and turn without world-loading pauses.

steps.action: Create the shears-use scoreboard objective exactly as specified in the report. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that the objective named "shear" was created; no red command error is shown.

steps.action: Display the new objective in the right-side scoreboard slot. Press T, enter the command including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A sidebar headed "shear" appears on the right side of the game display, although the player's entry may not appear until a score is initialized.

steps.action: Initialize the current player's score to a visible baseline so that a before-trigger value is available. Press T, enter the command including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The sidebar lists the current player's name with a score of 0 under the "shear" objective.

steps.action: Obtain one fresh pair of shears without changing out of Survival mode. Press T, enter the version-compatible give command including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A new shears item appears in the player's inventory or hotbar and the command reports that one shears item was given.

steps.action: Obtain one white carpet for the deterministic carpet test. Press T, enter the command including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A white carpet item appears in the player's inventory or hotbar and the command reports that one white carpet was given.

steps.action: Put the white carpet into the hotbar if it is not already there. Press E to open the inventory, identify the white carpet, and move it into one of the nine bottom hotbar slots. Close the inventory with E, then select that slot using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E; move White Carpet to a hotbar slot; E; select that hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The item name "White Carpet" appears above the hotbar and the player's hand holds the carpet.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of a nearby full solid ground block, such as a grass block, dirt block, or stone block, and right-click once to place the white carpet on it.
steps.success_cue: A thin white carpet block is visibly placed on top of the selected solid block.

steps.action: Select the fresh shears. If they are not in the hotbar, press E, move the shears into a bottom hotbar slot, close the inventory with E, and select that slot using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: Select the hotbar slot containing Shears
steps.success_cue: The item name "Shears" appears above the hotbar and the shears are visible in the player's hand.

steps.action: Verify the final pre-trigger state without mining the carpet yet: the player is in Survival mode, the placed white carpet is within reach, the fresh shears are selected, and the "shear" sidebar still shows the initialized pre-trigger score.
steps.success_cue: The Survival hearts and hunger HUD are visible, the crosshair can be placed on the carpet, shears are held, and the "shear" objective remains displayed in the sidebar.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair directly at the placed white carpet and use the attack/mine control while continuing to hold the shears. With default controls, left-click or briefly hold left-click until that single carpet block is completely mined. Do not mine another block afterward.
steps.exact_input: left-click the white carpet while holding Shears
steps.success_cue: The placed carpet has been removed and its dropped carpet item is visible on the ground or has been collected; no second block has been mined.

stor.handoff_condition: The single white carpet block has just been mined once in Survival mode while the fresh shears were selected, and the "shear" scoreboard objective is still displayed. Hand control immediately to the observation subsystem before using the shears or mining any additional block.
uncertainties: The report says "carpet" without specifying a color. White carpet is selected only as a deterministic representative; no color-specific condition is stated.

The report lists tall_grass, large_fern, seagrass, tall_seagrass, and nether_sprouts as additional affected blocks, but reproducing every listed variant is not required for the minimum path. This plan uses carpet because the report explicitly describes mining carpet with shears.

The command that sets the player's score to 0 is an added baseline-initialization step and is not part of the report's original command list. It is used so the sidebar has a visible pre-trigger value.
No seed, coordinates, biome, difficulty setting, dedicated-server requirement, or multiplayer requirement is supplied by the report.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-273932:"Times Used" statistic for watter bottles increases by 2 when converting dirt to mud in creative
source_meta._title: "minecraft.used:minecraft.potion" increases by a value of two when using water bottles to create mud in creative mode

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 22w11a in a fresh single-player world with commands available. The statistic-triggering interaction must be performed in Creative mode. Default keyboard and mouse controls are assumed; use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.
preconditions: Launch the exact recommended affected version, Java Edition 22w11a.
Use a fresh single-player world so that the scoreboard objective does not already exist and earlier potion use cannot complicate the baseline.
Enable commands when creating the world. One deterministic option is to create the world in Survival mode with Allow Cheats set to ON, then switch to Creative mode during the procedure.
Wait until the world and surrounding chunks have loaded and movement responds normally.
Ensure there is an ordinary solid surface on which a standard Dirt block can be placed.
After creating the objective, do not use any potion item until the single water-bottle interaction specified by the trigger step.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition 22w11a, create or open the prepared fresh single-player world, and wait for loading to finish.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the loaded world, nearby terrain is rendered, movement responds normally, and commands are available.

steps.action: Open in-game chat by pressing T. Enter the report's objective-creation command exactly as provided, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat displays a command-success message indicating that the scoreboard objective named UseWaterBottle was created. There is no message saying that the objective already exists or that the command is invalid.

steps.action: Open chat again with T. Enter the report's sidebar-display command exactly as provided, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The scoreboard sidebar for UseWaterBottle is visible on the right side of the game screen. The player may have no displayed score yet because the tracked item has not been used.

steps.action: Switch the player to Creative mode. Open chat with T, enter the game-mode command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A game-mode update message confirms Creative mode. The player has the Creative inventory and can fly by double-tapping Space.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory control, which is E by default, and select the Search Items tab—the tab containing a text search field.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open and its item search field is available.

steps.action: Click the Creative inventory search field, clear any existing text, and type "dirt". Locate the item whose tooltip is exactly "Dirt", excluding Coarse Dirt, Rooted Dirt, Grass Block, and other variants. Left-click Dirt to pick up a stack, then left-click an empty hotbar slot in the bottom row to place it there.
steps.success_cue: A standard Dirt stack is present in one of the nine hotbar slots at the bottom of the inventory.

steps.action: Return to the search field, clear the previous search text, and type "water bottle". Locate the ordinary drinkable item whose tooltip is "Water Bottle". Do not select a Splash Water Bottle, Lingering Water Bottle, or another potion. Left-click the Water Bottle, then left-click a different empty hotbar slot to place it there.
steps.success_cue: An ordinary Water Bottle is present in the hotbar in a slot different from the Dirt stack.

steps.action: Close the Creative inventory by pressing E or Escape.
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible again, with both Dirt and the Water Bottle shown in separate hotbar slots and the UseWaterBottle sidebar still displayed.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing Dirt by pressing its corresponding number key, 1 through 9, or by scrolling until the Dirt slot is highlighted.
steps.exact_input: Hotbar key 1-9 corresponding to the Dirt slot
steps.success_cue: Dirt is shown in the player's main hand and its hotbar slot has the active-slot highlight.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at an exposed face of an existing solid block with enough empty space beside it, then right-click once to place one Dirt block.
steps.success_cue: One standard Dirt block is placed in the world, is within interaction reach, and has at least one exposed face that can be targeted.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the ordinary Water Bottle using its corresponding number key, 1 through 9, or by scrolling until that slot is highlighted.
steps.exact_input: Hotbar key 1-9 corresponding to the Water Bottle slot
steps.success_cue: The Water Bottle is visible in the player's main hand and its hotbar slot has the active-slot highlight.

steps.action: Position the crosshair directly over an exposed face of the placed Dirt block. Do not right-click yet. Confirm that the UseWaterBottle objective remains displayed in the sidebar; if no player score is listed yet, leave it uninitialized rather than issuing any additional scoreboard command.
steps.success_cue: The player is in Creative mode, the Water Bottle is selected, the crosshair targets the placed Dirt block, and the UseWaterBottle sidebar is visible immediately before the only tracked use action.

steps.action: With the crosshair still targeting the placed Dirt block, use the selected Water Bottle on that block exactly once by pressing the use-item control, which is right-click by default. Do not perform a second click.
steps.success_cue: The single water-bottle use interaction has completed and the targeted Dirt block has converted into Mud; no additional potion-use interaction has been made.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just right-clicked exactly once with an ordinary Water Bottle on the placed Dirt block in Creative mode, the block has converted into Mud, and the UseWaterBottle objective remains displayed in the sidebar. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately, before any further use-item action.
uncertainties: The report supplies no world seed, coordinates, world type, or server requirement. A fresh single-player world and any convenient buildable location are therefore used as deterministic practical choices.
The report says to switch into Creative mode but does not prescribe a method or starting game mode. Starting with commands enabled and executing /gamemode creative is used as the operational method.

The report does not require an explicit pre-trigger score value. In a fresh world, the sidebar may contain only the objective title until the first tracked use; the plan intentionally avoids modifying the statistic with an extra scoreboard command.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-302587:“minecraft.used:minecraft.ITEM” doesn't increase when placing items onto shelves
source_meta._title: minecraft.used:minecraft.BOOK_TYPE doesn't increase when placing books onto chiseled bookshelves

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 22w42a in a newly created single-player Overworld; Creative mode; cheats enabled; the built-in Update 1.20 experimental data pack enabled during world creation; vanilla client; default mouse and keyboard controls assumed unless equivalent rebound controls are used.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher is configured to make historical Java Edition snapshots available, and snapshot 22w42a can be launched.
Use a new world rather than an existing world because the experimental feature toggle needed for the chiseled bookshelf must be selected during world creation.
Do not use fix version 1.19.3 Pre-release 1 for this reproduction.
Use a player with permission to execute scoreboard commands; Creative single-player with cheats enabled satisfies this requirement.
Leave the newly placed chiseled bookshelf empty until the final trigger interaction.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation that runs Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 22w42a, launch it, and wait for the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu identifies the running version as snapshot 22w42a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and ensure Allow Cheats is ON. No particular world seed is required by the report.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen is configured for Creative mode with commands permitted.

steps.action: Before creating the world, open the Data Packs screen. Locate the built-in experimental pack labeled Update 1.20 or update_1_20 and move it from the available list to the selected/enabled list, then choose Done.
steps.success_cue: The built-in Update 1.20 data pack is shown in the selected/enabled data-pack list.

steps.action: Create the world. If an experimental-features warning appears, confirm that you want to proceed. Wait until terrain has rendered and movement and commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the newly created Overworld, surrounding chunks are rendered, and the game responds normally to movement.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the report's first command exactly, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command completes without a red syntax or permission error and the UseWritableBook scoreboard objective exists.

steps.action: Press T to open chat again. Enter the report's second command exactly, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A sidebar headed UseWritableBook is visible on the right side of the screen. The player's row may remain absent until the criterion first receives a score.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab to locate a Book and Quill, a Lectern, and a Chiseled Bookshelf. Drag one of each into separate slots in the hotbar, which is the nine-slot row at the bottom of the inventory, then close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.exact_input: Book and Quill; Lectern; Chiseled Bookshelf
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains one Book and Quill, one Lectern, and one Chiseled Bookshelf.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Lectern by pressing its corresponding number key or scrolling the mouse wheel until the lectern is outlined in the hotbar.
steps.success_cue: The Lectern is shown as the held item and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of a solid floor block with open space above it and right-click once to place the lectern.
steps.success_cue: A lectern is standing on the floor with its slanted top accessible to the player.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Chiseled Bookshelf.
steps.success_cue: The Chiseled Bookshelf is shown as the held block and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of a nearby solid floor block and right-click once to place the chiseled bookshelf. Keep its slotted front face exposed and reachable, and do not insert any books yet.
steps.success_cue: A newly placed, empty chiseled bookshelf is near the lectern, and its front face can be directly targeted.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Book and Quill. This item is the writable book tracked by minecraft.used:minecraft.writable_book.
steps.success_cue: The Book and Quill is visible in the player's main hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim at the placed lectern and right-click once with the Book and Quill to put the writable book onto the lectern.
steps.success_cue: The lectern visibly holds an open book and the Book and Quill is no longer held in the player's hand.

steps.action: Return to normal world view so the sidebar can be inspected. If a book interface opened automatically, press Esc or use its Done control without signing the book.
steps.exact_input: Esc, if a book interface is open
steps.success_cue: The player is back in world view, the book remains on the lectern, and the UseWritableBook sidebar is visible.

steps.action: Read and record the numeric UseWritableBook sidebar score now shown beside the player's name. This is the pre-trigger reference value for the later observation.
steps.success_cue: The player's numeric UseWritableBook score after the lectern interaction has been recorded.

steps.action: Aim at the occupied lectern and right-click to open its book interface.
steps.success_cue: The lectern's book interface is open and provides a control for taking the book.

steps.action: Click the Take Book control in the lectern interface to retrieve the writable book.
steps.success_cue: The interface closes or updates, the lectern is empty, and the Book and Quill has returned to the player's inventory.

steps.action: If the recovered Book and Quill is not already in the active hotbar slot, press E, locate it in the player inventory, move it into a hotbar slot if necessary, close the inventory, and select that slot.
steps.success_cue: The recovered Book and Quill is once again visible in the player's main hand, while the chiseled bookshelf remains empty.

steps.action: Aim at the exposed front face of the empty chiseled bookshelf and right-click exactly once with the Book and Quill to insert it. Do not perform another interaction after this click.
steps.success_cue: The Book and Quill is visibly stored in the chiseled bookshelf and the trigger interaction has completed.

stor.handoff_condition: The writable Book and Quill has just been inserted into the previously empty chiseled bookshelf with one right-click, the pre-trigger UseWritableBook sidebar score from the lectern control has been recorded, and no additional interaction has occurred. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, seed, or server requirement. This plan uses a new Creative single-player world with cheats as the simplest deterministic environment for obtaining the blocks and running the supplied commands.

Snapshot 22w42a places the chiseled bookshelf behind the built-in Update 1.20 experimental data pack. The pack therefore has to be enabled while creating the new world; the exact displayed capitalization may vary with the client language.

The description names book, writable_book, and written_book objectives, but the supplied Steps to Reproduce provide an exact command only for minecraft.used:minecraft.writable_book. This plan follows that supplied writable-book variant and does not add separate plain-book or written-book trials.

The report does not explicitly describe retrieving the writable book from the lectern, but its wording subsequently reuses the writable book. This plan retrieves and reselects the same item through the Java Edition lectern interface.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-277152:The statistic for killing a creaking doesn't increment when breaking a creaking heart
source_meta._title: The statistics screen does not visually differentiate the creaking and creaking_transient entities

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 24w40a in a new single-player Creative-mode world using the integrated server, with commands permitted, the Winter Drop experiment enabled, a non-Peaceful difficulty, mob spawning enabled, and no gameplay-altering mods or resource packs.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected snapshot 24w40a rather than the fixed version 24w46a.
Use a newly created world so that the player's mob statistics begin without pre-existing Creaking records.

Enable the Winter Drop experiment on the Experiments screen while creating the world; this experiment supplies the Pale Oak, Creaking, and Creaking Heart content in 24w40a. ([feedback.minecraft.net](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/30738932967053-Minecraft-Java-Edition-Snapshot-24w40a?utm_source=openai))
Permit in-game commands. Creative mode is selected as a practical setup choice because the report does not specify a game mode and the required blocks can then be obtained without exploration.
Keep the difficulty above Peaceful and keep the doMobSpawning gamerule enabled so the Creaking Heart can create its associated entity.
Use the default mouse bindings unless controls were intentionally rebound: left-click attacks or breaks, right-click uses or places, E opens inventory, T opens chat, and Esc opens the pause menu.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation for snapshot 24w40a, launch it, and wait for the title screen to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running Java Edition version as 24w40a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then Create New World. Set Game Mode to Creative. Ensure commands are allowed if the creation screen exposes a separate command-permission option.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is configured for Creative mode with command access.

steps.action: Before creating the world, open the Experiments screen, switch Winter Drop to ON, and confirm any experimental-feature warning without leaving the creation process.
steps.success_cue: Winter Drop is shown as enabled on the world-creation screen. The experiment is required to expose the Creaking content in 24w40a. ([feedback.minecraft.net](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/30738932967053-Minecraft-Java-Edition-Snapshot-24w40a?utm_source=openai))

steps.action: Create the world. Do not begin setup until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the loaded world, nearby chunks are rendered, and normal movement is responsive.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, type the difficulty command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that the difficulty is Normal.

steps.action: Press T, enter the gamerule command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports that doMobSpawning is now true.

steps.action: Move to a reasonably flat, open construction site with several blocks of unobstructed ground around it. Avoid building under a low ceiling or directly beside unrelated mobs. Keep this area loaded for the remainder of the reproduction.
steps.success_cue: There is clear ground for a three-block-tall column and open nearby space in which a Creaking can appear.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab to obtain one Netherite Sword, at least two Pale Oak Logs, and one Creaking Heart. Place all three item types into hotbar slots; the hotbar is the row of nine slots at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.exact_input: Netherite Sword; Pale Oak Log; Creaking Heart
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains a sword, at least two Pale Oak Logs, and one Creaking Heart.

steps.action: Close the inventory. Stand at the open test site, press T, type the report's summon command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback indicates a successful summon and an artificial Creaking is visible near the player.

steps.action: Select the Netherite Sword in the active hotbar slot using its number key or the mouse wheel. Approach within attack range, center the crosshair on the summoned Creaking, and left-click to kill it. Wait for its death animation to finish; attack again only if the first attack did not remove it.
steps.success_cue: The command-summoned Creaking has completed its death animation and is no longer present.

steps.action: Select a Pale Oak Log in the hotbar. Aim at the top surface of a flat ground block and right-click once to place the lower log upright.
steps.success_cue: One upright Pale Oak Log is present on the ground at the construction site.

steps.action: Select the Creaking Heart. Aim at the center of the lower log's top face and right-click once, placing the heart directly on top of that log.
steps.success_cue: A Creaking Heart occupies the block immediately above the lower Pale Oak Log.

steps.action: Select the second Pale Oak Log. Aim at the Creaking Heart's top face and right-click once so the second log is directly above the heart. Placing both logs through their top or bottom faces keeps their axes vertical and aligned with the heart.
steps.success_cue: A vertical three-block column exists in this order from bottom to top: Pale Oak Log, Creaking Heart, Pale Oak Log. The two logs are aligned along the same vertical axis, satisfying the reported heart arrangement. ([feedback.minecraft.net](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/30738932967053-Minecraft-Java-Edition-Snapshot-24w40a?utm_source=openai))

steps.action: Move approximately 8 to 12 blocks away from the column while keeping it and the surrounding ground within render distance. Do not leave or unload the area.
steps.success_cue: The player is no longer touching the structure, but the column and nearby spawning area remain loaded and visible.

steps.action: Press T, type the report's time command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms the time change and the world is visibly at night.

steps.action: Remain near the column and scan the open ground around it. Wait without changing the time or breaking the structure until the Creaking Heart creates a Creaking. Do not continue merely because the heart is present; continue only after the entity itself appears.
steps.success_cue: A living, wooden humanoid Creaking associated with the heart is visible near the column. Creaking Hearts activate at night when positioned between correctly aligned Pale Oak Logs. ([feedback.minecraft.net](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/30738932967053-Minecraft-Java-Edition-Snapshot-24w40a?utm_source=openai))

steps.action: While the heart-spawned Creaking remains loaded, press T and enter the report's damage command exactly, including the leading slash, selector, entity identifier, damage type, amount, and attribution to @s. Press Enter once. If the command reports that no entity was found, do not proceed to statistics; return to the previous wait condition and execute the command once after the entity is present.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted, reports that damage was applied to the selected creaking_transient, and the targeted heart-spawned Creaking begins its removal or death sequence.

steps.action: Wait until the targeted Creaking has finished its removal or death sequence and normal player input remains responsive. Do not damage additional Creakings.
steps.success_cue: The targeted heart-spawned Creaking is no longer present and both report-specified kill actions have been completed exactly once.

steps.action: Press Esc to open the pause menu, then click Statistics. Wait for the Statistics screen to load.
steps.success_cue: The Statistics screen is open and its category controls are responsive. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AMenu_screen/Java_Edition?utm_source=openai))

steps.action: Select the Mobs statistics category, represented by the Mobs tab or mob-face icon, and scroll as needed until the Creaking-related statistics entries produced by the two completed kills are in the visible portion of the list. Stop interacting as soon as that section is visible.
steps.success_cue: The Mobs statistics section containing the Creaking-related records is on screen and ready for visual inspection by the Observation Agent; no conclusion about the entries has been made.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has completed one player-attributed kill of the command-summoned creaking and one player-attributed out-of-world damage removal of the heart-spawned creaking_transient, then opened the Mobs statistics category and brought the Creaking-related entries into view. Begin visual observation of those entries without further player input.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a seed, coordinates, world preset, game mode, or server type. This plan uses a new single-player Creative world and an arbitrary open construction site as the minimum deterministic setup.

The report says only that the Creaking Heart must be between two correctly aligned Pale Oak Logs. The plan implements this as a vertical log-heart-log column, with all three blocks aligned on the Y axis.
The report does not state a required difficulty or gamerule value. Normal difficulty and doMobSpawning=true are practical safeguards against preventing the heart-created entity from appearing.
The exact position of the Mobs category control and Creaking entries can vary with window dimensions and GUI scale, so scrolling may be required.
External snapshot documentation describes the experiment and heart activation conditions, but the report remains the source of truth for the exact summon, time, and damage commands.

source_meta._title: "minecraft.used:minecraft.trident" doesn't increase when throwing a trident

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 24w44a in a single-player world. Use Creative mode for deterministic item acquisition and enable commands/cheats so the two scoreboard commands from the report can be executed. No dedicated server or additional players are required.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected version 24w44a rather than the fixed version 24w45a.
Create or open a single-player world with commands/cheats enabled.
Use Creative mode as a practical way to obtain an ordinary trident without adding enchantments.
The test trident must not have the Riptide enchantment.
Use a newly created scoreboard objective named exactly MC-278071 so prior scores do not affect the test.
Use the commands from the report exactly and in the listed order.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft: Java Edition 24w44a from the Minecraft Launcher, then create or open a single-player world with commands enabled. For the simplest setup, select Creative mode when creating the world; if using an existing world without cheats, open the pause menu, select Open to LAN, set Allow Cheats to ON, and start the LAN world.
steps.success_cue: The player is loaded into a responsive world in version 24w44a and can execute commands.

steps.action: Press T to open the in-game chat and command input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's first command, including the leading slash, and press Enter to create the scoreboard objective that tracks uses of a trident.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that the scoreboard objective MC-278071 was created. If the game says the objective already exists, remove the old objective or use a fresh world, then execute this exact command again before continuing.

steps.action: Press T to open chat again, enter the report's second command including the leading slash, and press Enter to display the objective in the scoreboard sidebar.
steps.success_cue: The MC-278071 objective is assigned to the sidebar display. The player's name may not yet be listed because no score has been recorded for the new objective.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory by pressing E. Use the Search Items tab or locate the Combat items, find Trident, and place one ordinary trident into any hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the inventory and gameplay screen.
steps.success_cue: An ordinary trident is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Hover the pointer over the trident and inspect its tooltip. Ensure that the trident is not enchanted with Riptide; a newly obtained ordinary Creative inventory trident should have no enchantment text. Close the inventory by pressing E.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed and the available test trident has no Riptide enchantment.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the trident by pressing its number key, 1 through 9, or by scrolling the mouse wheel until that slot is highlighted.
steps.success_cue: The trident is visible in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted as the active slot.

steps.action: Aim toward an unobstructed patch of ground or a nearby solid wall so the trident can be thrown safely without requiring combat or a target entity.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair points at a clear destination where the thrown trident can visibly travel and land.

steps.action: Press and hold the Use Item control, which is right-click by default, long enough to fully charge the trident throw. Do not release the control yet.
steps.success_cue: The player is holding the trident in its charged throwing pose.

steps.action: Release the Use Item control, right-click by default, once the trident is charged. Perform this throw only once.
steps.success_cue: The trident leaves the player's hand as a projectile and travels toward the aimed location. The throw action is complete.

steps.action: Wait only until the thrown trident has visibly landed or stopped moving and normal player input remains responsive. Do not throw another trident or pick up and reuse it before observation.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one non-Riptide trident throw has been completed, and the game is ready for the scoreboard and statistics values to be inspected.

steps.action: Leave the scoreboard sidebar visible and pause the game by pressing Esc. Select Statistics from the pause menu and wait for the statistics screen to load.
steps.success_cue: The Statistics screen is open after the single trident throw.

steps.action: Select the Items tab in the Statistics screen. Locate the Trident entry in the item statistics list, using the list's scrolling or filtering controls if necessary, but do not interpret or report its value yet.
steps.success_cue: The Items statistics tab is open and the Trident statistics entry is available for the observation subsystem to inspect; the MC-278071 sidebar can also be inspected after closing the menu.

stor.handoff_condition: One ordinary trident without Riptide has just been thrown exactly once while the MC-278071 scoreboard objective tracks minecraft.used:minecraft.trident. The Items tab of the Statistics screen is open at the Trident entry. Hand control to the observation subsystem to inspect the statistic, then close the menu if needed to inspect the MC-278071 sidebar value.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is selected only as a deterministic way to obtain an unenchanted trident; it is not asserted as a required condition of the bug.
The report does not specify whether the world is single-player or multiplayer. A command-enabled single-player world is used because no server-only or multi-player condition is described.
A newly created objective may omit the player's name from the sidebar until the player has a recorded score; absence of a pre-trigger row should not prevent execution of the trident throw.
